title: Area and perimeter of an L-shape
subject: math

objectives.text: Split an L-shape into two rectangles and add their areas to find the total area
successCriteria: I can split the L into part A and part B and find each area
I can add 24 000 and 16 800 to get the total area of 40 800
assessmentPoints: Split answers in the opening activity
Responses when the box trap is sprung in the third activity

objectives.text: Find the perimeter of an L-shape by adding all six edge lengths, including the inner steps
successCriteria: I can name all six edges of the L, including the inner steps
I can add the six edges to get the perimeter of 920
assessmentPoints: Edge answers in the perimeter activity
Worksheet answers in the closing practice

activities.title: Two rectangles make one L: split and add the areas
Trace the edge: walk all six sides for the perimeter

differentiation.support: Provide a cut-out L on grid paper so the empty corner can be seen before it is discussed.

activities.title: Land the add-the-parts and walk-every-side rule

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why the 200 by 260 box overcounts the area of the L.
